category: Phrasal verbs on regular bases: M-P

entries.meaning: To send something to an office or a company by mail. ---
examples: Mail in the rebate form within thirty days or you lose it.
She mailed her ballot in two weeks early.
Half the applications were mailed in after the deadline.
entries.русский: отправлять по почте, отправить по почте; высылать, выслать
entries.separable: separable — mail in the form, mail the form in, and with a pronoun it must split: mail it in, never ✗ mail in it.
entries.forms: mail in · mailed in · mailed in

entries.meaning: To do something with no real effort, just enough to get through it. ---
examples: The band mailed it in for the last three songs.
You can tell he's mailing it in until his contract runs out.
They mail it in every year against the weaker teams.
entries.русский: халтурить, схалтурить; делать спустя рукава
entries.separable: fixed — the object is always it and nothing else can go there: they mailed it in, never ✗ mailed the concert in. Informal.
entries.forms: mail it in · mailed it in · mailed it in
entries.third person: mails it in · -ing form: mailing it in
entries.transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object it

entries.meaning: To stop complaining and face something difficult bravely. ---
examples: Man up and tell her the truth.
He finally manned up and apologized to the whole team.
She told everybody to man up and take the loss.
entries.русский: брать себя в руки, взять себя в руки; собираться с духом, собраться с духом
entries.separable: nothing to separate — the verb takes no object at all: man up and call her. Informal, and plenty of speakers now find it dated.
entries.forms: man up · manned up · manned up

entries.meaning: To plan something in careful detail, step by step. ---
examples: We mapped out the whole trip on a napkin.
She's mapping out her first two years of classes.
The strategy was mapped out long before the vote.
entries.русский: намечать, наметить; планировать, распланировать
entries.separable: separable — map out a plan, map the whole route out, map it out.
entries.forms: map out · mapped out · mapped out

entries.meaning: To give someone a lower grade or score because of a fault. ---
examples: That professor marks you down for every late paper.
I got marked down for not citing my sources.
The judges were marking down anyone who stepped out of bounds.
entries.русский: снижать оценку, снизить оценку; снимать баллы
entries.separable: separable — the teacher marked me down, marked down two students. The reason follows with for: marked down for spelling.
entries.forms: mark down · marked down · marked down

entries.meaning: To lower the price of something, usually to sell it faster. ---
examples: They marked down everything in the store after the holidays.
The sofa was marked down from nine hundred dollars to five.
They're marking the summer stock down again this week.
entries.русский: уценивать, уценить; снижать цену, снизить цену
entries.separable: separable — mark down the winter coats, mark the coats down, mark them down.
entries.forms: mark down · marked down · marked down

entries.meaning: To put a mark beside something on a list to show it is done. ---
examples: She marks off every chore as she finishes it.
He marked the last box off and went home.
I've marked off three of the five apartments we looked at.
entries.русский: отмечать, отметить (в списке); вычёркивать, вычеркнуть
entries.separable: separable — mark off each item, mark each item off, mark it off.
entries.forms: mark off · marked off · marked off

entries.meaning: To cover a text or a drawing with corrections and notes. ---
examples: My editor marks up everything I send her.
He marked the blueprint up before the meeting.
She's marking up my essay right now.
entries.русский: размечать, разметить; делать пометки, исписать правками
entries.separable: separable — mark up the draft, mark the draft up, mark it up.
entries.forms: mark up · marked up · marked up

entries.meaning: To raise the price of something well above what it cost. ---
examples: The gallery marks up every print by three hundred percent.
Restaurants mark wine up far more than food.
Those jackets have been marked up twice since spring.
entries.русский: повышать цену, повысить цену; делать наценку
entries.separable: separable — mark up the prices, mark the prices up, mark them up.
entries.forms: mark up · marked up · marked up

entries.meaning: To become part of a family, class, or fortune by marrying someone who already belongs to it. ---
examples: She married into one of the oldest families in the state.
Having married into a farming family, he learned to drive a tractor at forty.
You don't just marry into that kind of money.
entries.русский: входить, войти (в семью, в круг — через брак)
entries.separable: inseparable — the family or the money follows into: marry into a fortune.
entries.forms: marry into · married into · married into

entries.meaning: To arrange a marriage for someone, usually your own child. ---
examples: Her parents married her off at eighteen.
The family was determined to marry off all four daughters.
He's marrying his niece off to a business partner.
entries.русский: выдавать замуж, выдать замуж; женить
entries.separable: separable — marry off their daughters, and marry them off; with a pronoun it must split: marry her off, never ✗ marry off her.
entries.forms: marry off · married off · married off

entries.meaning: To agree with or correspond to something else. ---
examples: His story doesn't match up with the security footage.
The totals matched up to the penny.
Nothing in the report was matching up.
entries.русский: совпадать, совпасть; сходиться, сойтись
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the other thing follows with with: doesn't match up with the invoice.
entries.forms: match up · matched up · matched up

entries.meaning: To put two things together because they belong with each other. ---
examples: Match up each name with a photo.
She matched the receipts up with the charges on the card.
We're matching up mentors and students all week.
entries.русский: подбирать пару, подобрать; сопоставлять, сопоставить
entries.separable: separable — match up the socks, match the names up, match them up.
entries.forms: match up · matched up · matched up

entries.meaning: To use something all the way up to its limit. ---
examples: He maxed out two credit cards in a single month.
My retirement contribution is already maxed out for the year.
The free plan maxes out at five users.
entries.русский: исчерпывать, исчерпать (лимит); доводить до предела, довести до предела
entries.separable: separable when it has an object — max out the card, max the card out, max it out. It is also used with no object: the server maxed out at noon.
entries.forms: max out · maxed out · maxed out
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (he maxed out his credit card), intransitive (the plan maxes out at five users)

entries.meaning: To take an exact amount of something out of a larger supply. ---
examples: Measure out three tablespoons of oil.
He measured out the dog's food for the whole week.
She was measuring the coffee out when the phone rang.
entries.русский: отмерять, отмерить; отсчитывать, отсчитать
entries.separable: separable — measure out two cups, measure the flour out, measure it out.
entries.forms: measure out · measured out · measured out

entries.meaning: To be as good as people expect, or as good as someone else. ---
examples: The sequel just doesn't measure up.
He spent his whole career worrying that he'd never measure up to his older brother.
Two of the three finalists measured up; the third didn't.
entries.русский: соответствовать, оказаться на высоте; дотягивать, дотянуть
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the standard follows with to: measure up to his father, measure up to it.
entries.forms: measure up · measured up · measured up

entries.meaning: To disappear gradually until there is nothing left. ---
examples: His nerves melted away as soon as he started talking.
The crowd melted away after the last song.
Our lead was melting away in the fourth quarter.
entries.русский: таять, растаять; исчезать, исчезнуть; улетучиваться
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the subject is the thing that disappears: her anger melted away.
entries.forms: melt away · melted away · melted away

entries.meaning: To lose emotional control completely. ---
examples: The toddler melted down in the cereal aisle.
He melts down every time the wifi drops.
She was melting down halfway through the presentation.
entries.русский: срываться, сорваться; терять самообладание, потерять самообладание
entries.separable: nothing to separate — in this sense there is no object: he melted down on live television. The noun is one word: a meltdown.
entries.forms: melt down · melted down · melted down

entries.meaning: To waste time or behave in a silly, unserious way. ---
examples: Stop messing around and finish your homework.
We messed around in the parking lot until the doors opened.
He messes around all week and then panics on Sunday night.
entries.русский: бездельничать, валять дурака; дурачиться
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object: quit messing around. (British English says mess about for the same thing.)
entries.forms: mess around · messed around · messed around

entries.meaning: To handle or tinker with something, often without really knowing how it works. ---
examples: Don't mess around with the thermostat.
He messed around with the code all afternoon and broke the build.
She's been messing around with watercolors since she retired.
entries.русский: возиться с, повозиться с; копаться в, лезть в
entries.separable: inseparable — the object follows the whole phrase: mess around with the settings, mess around with them. ✗ mess the settings around with.
entries.forms: mess around with · messed around with · messed around with
entries.third person: messes around with · -ing form: messing around with

entries.meaning: To make a mistake or do something badly. ---
examples: I'm sorry — I messed up.
He messes up whenever the coach is watching.
She was terrified of messing up in front of the whole class.
entries.русский: ошибаться, ошибиться; напортачить, оплошать
entries.separable: nothing to separate — in this sense the verb takes no object at all: I messed up, don't mess up.
entries.forms: mess up · messed up · messed up

entries.meaning: To make something dirty or untidy. ---
examples: The kids messed up the living room in five minutes.
The wind messed my hair up on the way over.
Who's been messing up my desk?
entries.русский: приводить в беспорядок, привести в беспорядок; пачкать, испачкать
entries.separable: separable — mess up the bed, mess the bed up, mess it up.
entries.forms: mess up · messed up · messed up

entries.meaning: To spoil or ruin something that was going well. ---
examples: The rain messed up our whole weekend.
One bad quarter messed the numbers up for the year.
Don't mess this up — we only get one try.
entries.русский: портить, испортить; срывать, сорвать
entries.separable: separable — mess up my plans, mess my plans up, mess them up.
entries.forms: mess up · messed up · messed up

entries.meaning: To interfere with something you were supposed to leave alone. ---
examples: Somebody messed with my seat adjustment.
Don't mess with the wiring unless the power is off.
Who's been messing with the file names?
entries.русский: трогать, тронуть; лезть в, влезть в; портить, испортить
entries.separable: inseparable — the object follows the whole phrase: someone messed with my settings, don't mess with it.
entries.forms: mess with · messed with · messed with

entries.meaning: To provoke or challenge someone who can make you regret it. ---
examples: Nobody messes with her older brother.
You picked the wrong guy to mess with.
He learned early not to be messing with the union.
entries.русский: связываться с, связаться с; задевать, задеть
entries.separable: inseparable — don't mess with him, never ✗ mess him with.
entries.forms: mess with · messed with · messed with

entries.meaning: To move about in a crowd with no clear purpose, usually while waiting. ---
examples: Fans were milling around the lobby an hour before the doors opened.
We milled around outside until somebody found the key.
A few reporters still mill around the courthouse every morning.
entries.русский: толпиться, слоняться; бродить без дела
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object: a crowd was milling around outside. (Mill about is the same verb.)
entries.forms: mill around · milled around · milled around

entries.meaning: To lose a chance to do or have something good. ---
examples: Come with us — you'll miss out otherwise.
I missed out on the early-bird price by one day.
She feels like she's missing out on the best years of her kids' lives.
entries.русский: упускать, упустить (возможность); оставаться в стороне, остаться в стороне
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no direct object; what you lose follows with on: missed out on the trip, missed out on it. ✗ missed the trip out.
entries.forms: miss out · missed out · missed out

entries.meaning: To add an ingredient and stir until it disappears into the rest. ---
examples: Mix in the flour a little at a time.
He mixed the berries in at the very end.
Once the butter is mixed in, the dough comes together fast.
entries.русский: вмешивать, вмешать; подмешивать, подмешать; добавлять, добавить
entries.separable: separable — mix in the eggs, mix the eggs in, mix them in.
entries.forms: mix in · mixed in · mixed in

entries.meaning: To change your usual routine so that things stay interesting. ---
examples: Let's mix it up and take the coast road this time.
The coach mixed it up in the second half and ran the ball.
She mixes it up every week so the class never gets boring.
entries.русский: разнообразить, внести разнообразие; менять подход, поменять подход
entries.separable: fixed — the object is always it: let's mix it up. No other noun can go there in this sense.
entries.forms: mix it up · mixed it up · mixed it up
entries.third person: mixes it up · -ing form: mixing it up
entries.transitivity: transitive — but only with the fixed object it

entries.meaning: To make something by stirring ingredients together. ---
examples: She mixed up a pitcher of lemonade and took it out to the porch.
He's mixing up pancake batter.
I mix up a big bowl of dressing every Sunday.
entries.русский: замешивать, замешать; разводить, развести; готовить, приготовить (смесь)
entries.separable: separable — mix up a batch of batter, mix a batch up. Careful: mix it up on its own usually means 'do something differently'.
entries.forms: mix up · mixed up · mixed up

entries.meaning: To mistake one thing or person for another. ---
examples: I always mix up his two sisters.
The pharmacy mixed the prescriptions up.
Our bags got mixed up at the airport.
entries.русский: путать, перепутать; путать местами, перепутать местами
entries.separable: separable — mix up the twins, mix the twins up, and with a pronoun it must split: I always mix them up, never ✗ mix up them.
entries.forms: mix up · mixed up · mixed up

entries.meaning: To fool around, or to fiddle with something you should leave alone. ---
examples: Quit monkeying around and get in the car.
He monkeyed around with the printer settings and now nothing works.
Those two monkey around in the back of the class all period.
entries.русский: дурачиться, валять дурака; возиться, повозиться
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; what you fiddle with follows with with: monkeying around with the carburetor.
entries.forms: monkey around · monkeyed around · monkeyed around

entries.meaning: To finish off the last small part of a job or a fight. ---
examples: Two of us stayed late to mop up the last of the paperwork.
Their closer mopped up the ninth inning in eleven pitches.
Troops spent another week mopping up pockets of resistance.
entries.русский: доделывать, доделать; добивать, добить (остатки)
entries.separable: separable — mop up the last few claims, mop them up.
entries.forms: mop up · mopped up · mopped up

entries.meaning: To soak up spilled liquid with a cloth or a mop. ---
examples: He mopped up the milk before it reached the rug.
Mop that up before somebody slips.
She's still mopping up after the pipe burst.
entries.русский: вытирать, вытереть; подтирать, подтереть
entries.separable: separable — mop up the spill, mop the spill up, mop it up.
entries.forms: mop up · mopped up · mopped up

entries.meaning: To go about looking sad and doing nothing, feeling sorry for yourself. ---
examples: He moped around the house for a week after the breakup.
Stop moping around and call her.
She mopes around every Sunday night before work.
entries.русский: хандрить, слоняться в унынии; кукситься
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object, though a place can follow around: moped around the house all day.
entries.forms: mope around · moped around · moped around

entries.meaning: To grow larger and larger bit by bit, usually about costs or problems. ---
examples: Small charges mount up fast on that card.
The medical bills mounted up while he was out of work.
Complaints have been mounting up since the redesign.
entries.русский: накапливаться, накопиться; расти, вырасти
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the subject is the thing piling up: the bills mounted up.
entries.forms: mount up · mounted up · mounted up

entries.meaning: To talk back rudely and disrespectfully. ---
examples: He got benched for mouthing off to the coach.
Don't mouth off to your mother.
She mouthed off one time too many and lost the job.
entries.русский: дерзить, надерзить; хамить, нахамить
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the person takes to and the subject takes about: mouthed off to the ref about a call.
entries.forms: mouth off · mouthed off · mouthed off

entries.meaning: To keep going instead of stopping, or to keep making steady progress. ---
examples: The officer told the crowd to move along.
The line moved along faster than I expected.
Things are moving along nicely on the remodel.
entries.русский: проходить, пройти (не задерживаясь); продвигаться, продвинуться
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object: move along, folks.
entries.forms: move along · moved along · moved along

entries.meaning: To change where you live again and again. ---
examples: We moved around a lot when I was a kid — six schools in nine years.
Army families move around every couple of years.
After college he kept moving around until he landed in Denver.
entries.русский: переезжать с места на место, часто переезжать
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object: we moved around a lot.
entries.forms: move around · moved around · moved around

entries.meaning: To leave the town where you live and go live somewhere else. ---
examples: My best friend moved away in third grade.
They're moving away as soon as the house sells.
Half my class has moved away since graduation.
entries.русский: переезжать, переехать (в другой город); уезжать, уехать
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the place you leave takes from: moved away from Cleveland.
entries.forms: move away · moved away · moved away

entries.meaning: To return to live in a place where you used to live. ---
examples: After the divorce she moved back to Ohio.
He's moving back in with his parents to save money.
They moved back two years after leaving.
entries.русский: возвращаться, вернуться (жить на прежнее место)
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object: moved back to Texas, moved back in with her parents.
entries.forms: move back · moved back · moved back

entries.meaning: To go ahead with a plan instead of waiting or stopping. ---
examples: The board voted to move forward with the merger.
We moved forward without waiting for legal.
Nothing is moving forward until the funding clears.
entries.русский: продвигаться, продвинуться; приступать, приступить (к делу)
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the plan follows with with: move forward with the merger.
entries.forms: move forward · moved forward · moved forward

entries.meaning: To come steadily closer, especially in order to attack or take control. ---
examples: SWAT moved in at four in the morning.
A storm is moving in from the west.
Federal agents move in only once the warrants are signed.
entries.русский: приближаться, приблизиться; наступать, надвигаться
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; to name the target add on: moved in on the building.
entries.forms: move in · moved in · moved in

entries.meaning: To start living in a new home. ---
examples: We moved in on the first of the month.
New neighbors are moving in downstairs.
She moved in with her boyfriend last spring.
entries.русский: вселяться, вселиться; въезжать, въехать
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the place takes to or into and a person takes with: moved in with her sister.
entries.forms: move in · moved in · moved in

entries.meaning: To close in on someone or something in order to seize or attack it. ---
examples: Police moved in on the house just before dawn.
A national chain is moving in on their customers.
They move in on a company the minute its stock slips.
entries.русский: подступать к, подступить к; посягать на, посягнуть на
entries.separable: inseparable — the object follows the whole phrase: moved in on the suspect, moved in on him. ✗ moved him in on.
entries.forms: move in on · moved in on · moved in on
entries.third person: moves in on · -ing form: moving in on

entries.meaning: To leave one subject or task and start the next one. ---
examples: Any questions? If not, let's move on.
We moved on to the budget after twenty minutes.
He kept moving on before anyone could answer.
entries.русский: переходить, перейти (к следующему); двигаться дальше
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; what comes next follows with to: move on to the next slide.
entries.forms: move on · moved on · moved on

entries.meaning: To stop being upset about something in the past and get on with your life. ---
examples: It took her a year to move on.
He's moved on — he's seeing somebody new.
You can't keep rereading his emails; you have to start moving on.
entries.русский: забывать, забыть (прошлое); начинать новую жизнь, начать новую жизнь
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; what you leave behind takes from: move on from a breakup.
entries.forms: move on · moved on · moved on

entries.meaning: To stop living in a place and take your things with you. ---
examples: He moved out the day the lease ended.
They're moving out at the end of the semester.
She's moved out twice and come back both times.
entries.русский: съезжать, съехать; выезжать, выехать
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; the place follows with of: moved out of the apartment.
entries.forms: move out · moved out · moved out

entries.meaning: To shift sideways so that someone else has room. ---
examples: Move over — there's room for one more.
He moved over so she could see the screen.
Everybody moved over one seat.
entries.русский: подвигаться, подвинуться; освобождать место, освободить место
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object: move over, could you move over a little?
entries.forms: move over · moved over · moved over

entries.meaning: To reschedule something for an earlier time or date. ---
examples: Can we move the meeting up to nine?
They moved up the launch by two weeks.
The wedding is being moved up because of his deployment.
entries.русский: переносить на более ранний срок, перенести на более ранний срок
entries.separable: separable — move up the meeting, move the meeting up, move it up.
entries.forms: move up · moved up · moved up

entries.meaning: To rise to a higher position, rank, or level. ---
examples: She moved up from intern to director in four years.
They moved him up to the varsity team.
Nobody in that department is moving up.
entries.русский: продвигаться, продвинуться (по службе); повышать, повысить
entries.separable: separable when it has an object — they moved her up to manager, moved him up. Most often there is no object at all: she moved up fast.
entries.forms: move up · moved up · moved up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (he moved up quickly), transitive (they moved her up a level)

entries.meaning: To knock down or kill people in numbers, with a vehicle or with gunfire. ---
examples: A drunk driver mowed down two cyclists on the shoulder.
The guns mowed them down as they crossed the field.
He's been mowing down hitters all season.
entries.русский: косить, скосить; сбивать, сбить (насмерть)
entries.separable: separable — mowed down two cyclists, mowed them down.
entries.forms: mow down · mowed down · mowed down

entries.meaning: To get to the end of something badly but somehow, without really knowing what you are doing. ---
examples: Neither of us reads music, so we just muddled through.
She muddled through the interview in her broken Spanish.
They're muddling through until the new director starts.
entries.русский: кое-как справляться, справиться; выкручиваться, выкрутиться
entries.separable: never split — usually there is no object at all (we muddled through), and when through takes one it follows the whole phrase: muddled through the interview. ✗ muddled the interview through.
entries.forms: muddle through · muddled through · muddled through
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (we muddled through), transitive (she muddled through the speech)

entries.meaning: To think about something slowly and carefully before deciding. ---
examples: Let me mull it over and call you tomorrow.
She mulled over the job offer for a solid week.
He's still mulling over whether to sell the house.
entries.русский: обдумывать, обдумать; размышлять над, взвешивать
entries.separable: separable — mull over the offer, mull the offer over, and with a pronoun it must split: let me mull it over, never ✗ mull over it.
entries.forms: mull over · mulled over · mulled over

entries.meaning: To force your way into something so as to take a share of what other people have. ---
examples: A national chain is muscling in on the local market.
He muscled in on a deal two other firms had spent a year building.
Nobody muscles in on that neighborhood.
entries.русский: влезать, влезть (силой); втираться, втереться
entries.separable: nothing to separate — no object; what you force your way into follows with on: muscled in on our territory.
entries.forms: muscle in · muscled in · muscled in

entries.meaning: To gather enough of a feeling or a quality to do something hard. ---
examples: It took him a month to muster up the nerve to ask.
She mustered up a smile and shook his hand.
They couldn't muster up enough votes to pass it.
entries.русский: собирать, собрать (силы, смелость); набираться, набраться (смелости)
entries.separable: separable, but in practice the object follows the particle — muster up the courage, muster up enough support. A pronoun can split it: he finally mustered it up.
entries.forms: muster up · mustered up · mustered up

entries.meaning: To find out or state something exactly, leaving nothing vague. ---
examples: Investigators still haven't nailed down the cause of the fire.
The report never nails down who approved the payment.
Once we've nailed it down, I'll email the whole team.

entries.meaning: To give a person or place the name of someone else, in that person's honor. ---

entries.meaning: To put something forward for other people to consider, use, or accept. ---

entries.meaning: To start talking honestly about your feelings or your private life. ---

entries.meaning: To ignore someone when deciding who gets a job or a promotion. ---

entries.meaning: To add even more of something, or to join everyone else in criticizing someone. ---

entries.meaning: To grow into a large amount, usually one nobody wanted. ---

Bills pile up fast when you're out sick.
Snow was piling up against the door.

entries.meaning: To show someone which person or thing you mean. ---

His toes were poking out of those old sneakers.
entries.русский: торчать; высовываться, высунуться; выглядывать, выглянуть
entries.separable: usually no object — the thing that shows is the subject: a sock was poking out of the bag. With a body part it separates: poke your head out, poke it out
entries.forms: poke out · poked out · poked out
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (a wire poked out), transitive (poked his head out the window)

entries.meaning: To finish something quickly and completely, especially food or a piece of work. ---
examples: He polished off three slices before anyone else sat down.
We can polish the rest of it off in the morning.
She is already polishing off her second bowl.
entries.русский: быстро съедать, съесть; приканчивать, прикончить; разделываться, разделаться (с делом)
entries.separable: separable — polish off the pizza, polish the pizza off, polish it off; never ✗ polish off it
entries.forms: polish off · polished off · polished off

entries.meaning: To improve a skill that has gone rusty, or a piece of work that is nearly done. ---
examples: I need to polish up my Spanish before the trip.
He polished the essay up over the weekend.
She has been polishing up her interview answers all week.
entries.русский: совершенствовать, усовершенствовать; подтягивать, подтянуть (навык); дорабатывать, доработать
entries.separable: separable — polish up your Spanish, polish your Spanish up, polish it up; never ✗ polish up it
entries.forms: polish up · polished up · polished up

entries.meaning: To hand over money you owe or would rather not pay, in informal American English. ---
examples: Everybody had to pony up twenty dollars for the gift.
He finally ponied up the deposit on Friday.
Nobody is ponying up for the repairs.
entries.русский: раскошеливаться, раскошелиться; выкладывать, выложить деньги
entries.separable: the money follows the whole verb — pony up forty bucks, pony up for the pizza; never ✗ pony forty bucks up. Just as often there is no object at all: somebody has to pony up
entries.forms: pony up · ponied up · ponied up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (we all ponied up), transitive (ponied up two hundred dollars)

entries.meaning: To visit somewhere for a very short time, usually without planning it. ---
examples: She popped in to say hello on her way home.
I will pop in after work if there is time.
He keeps popping in to check on the baby.
entries.русский: заглядывать, заглянуть (ненадолго); забегать, забежать
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the place takes at or to and the person you visit takes on: popped in at the office, popped in on my parents; never ✗ pop the office in
entries.forms: pop in · popped in · popped in

entries.meaning: To speak loudly and angrily, or to say more than you should. ---
examples: He popped off at the referee and got thrown out of the game.
Do not pop off about the layoffs until the memo goes out.
She is always popping off about how much better the old system was.
entries.русский: срываться, сорваться (на крик); возмущаться; трепать языком
entries.separable: inseparable — the person you are angry at takes at (popped off at the umpire), the subject takes about (popping off about taxes)
entries.forms: pop off · popped off · popped off

entries.meaning: To leave for a few minutes and come straight back. ---
examples: I am going to pop out for a sandwich.
She popped out for ten minutes and missed the call.
He is popping out to the bank before it closes.
entries.русский: выскакивать, выскочить (ненадолго); выбегать, выбежать
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the errand takes for and the place takes to: popped out for coffee, popping out to the bank; never ✗ pop the store out
entries.forms: pop out · popped out · popped out

entries.meaning: To appear suddenly, especially where you did not expect it. ---
examples: An ad popped up right in the middle of the video.
Her name pops up every time I search for the company.
Little coffee shops keep popping up all over downtown.
entries.русский: появляться, появиться внезапно; выскакивать, выскочить
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: the thing that appears is the subject. A window popped up, never ✗ the site popped up an ad
entries.forms: pop up · popped up · popped up

entries.meaning: To come along without warning, as a problem, an extra job or a chance does. ---
examples: Sorry, something popped up at work and I have to cancel.
If a cheaper flight pops up, book it right away.
Openings like that do not pop up very often.
entries.русский: возникать, возникнуть (неожиданно); подворачиваться, подвернуться
entries.separable: no object — intransitive: the problem or the opening is the subject. Something popped up at work, never ✗ they popped up a problem
entries.forms: pop up · popped up · popped up

entries.meaning: To read or study something long and closely. ---
examples: They pored over the contract line by line.
She pores over the sports page every morning.
We spent the night poring over old photographs.
entries.русский: изучать, изучить внимательно; корпеть (над); вчитываться, вчитаться
entries.separable: inseparable — over never lets go of its object: pored over the map, pored over it; never ✗ pored the map over
entries.forms: pore over · pored over · pored over

entries.meaning: To rain very hard. ---
examples: It poured down all afternoon and the game was called.
Rain pours down here for ten minutes and then stops.
It has been pouring down since six this morning.
entries.русский: лить как из ведра; хлестать (о дожде)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive, and the subject is rain or an empty it: it poured down all night; never ✗ pour the rain down
entries.forms: pour down · poured down · poured down

entries.meaning: To arrive in very large numbers or amounts all at once. ---
examples: Donations poured in after the story aired.
Messages are still pouring in.
Money pours in every December and dries up in January.
entries.русский: поступать, поступить в большом количестве; стекаться, стечься; хлынуть
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; a named destination takes into: donations poured into the fund; never ✗ pour the letters in
entries.forms: pour in · poured in · poured in

entries.meaning: To come out of a place in a steady stream, as a crowd does. ---
examples: Fans poured out of the arena after the final whistle.
Students pour out of that building at three every day.
People were pouring out onto the sidewalk.
entries.русский: валить, повалить (толпой); высыпать, высыпать (наружу)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive in this sense; the place you leave takes of: poured out of the arena; never ✗ pour the crowd out
entries.forms: pour out · poured out · poured out

entries.meaning: To let all of your feelings or troubles come out at once in words. ---
examples: She poured out the whole story before I could say a word.
He poured his heart out to a stranger on the plane.
They sat up all night pouring out their complaints.
entries.русский: изливать, излить (душу); выкладывать, выложить (всё)
entries.separable: separable — pour out your feelings, pour your feelings out, pour it all out; never ✗ pour out it. With heart the object sits in the middle: poured her heart out
entries.forms: pour out · poured out · poured out

entries.meaning: To switch a machine off in the proper way, rather than pulling the plug. ---
examples: Power down the machine before you unplug it.
They powered everything down ahead of the storm.
The whole system is powering down.
entries.русский: выключать, выключить (устройство); отключать, отключить
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — power down the server, power the server down, power it down; often there is no object: the system powers down at midnight
entries.forms: power down · powered down · powered down
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (power down the laptop), intransitive (the lab powers down at night)

entries.meaning: To keep going and finish something hard without stopping for a break. ---
examples: She powered through the last forty pages before midnight.
I am going to power through and finish tonight.
He is powering through a bad cold to get the report done.
entries.русский: осиливать, осилить; дожимать, дожать; продираться, продраться (через)
entries.separable: inseparable — through keeps its object: powered through the last chapter, powered through it; never ✗ powered the chapter through. It also works with no object at all: just power through
entries.forms: power through · powered through · powered through
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (power through the reading), intransitive (I will just power through)

entries.meaning: To switch a machine on and let it start running. ---
examples: Power up the projector before everyone gets here.
He powered the laptop up and waited two full minutes.
The generator is powering up now.
entries.русский: включать, включить (устройство); запускать, запустить
entries.separable: separable when there is an object — power up the laptop, power the laptop up, power it up; just as often there is no object: the tablet powers up in seconds
entries.forms: power up · powered up · powered up
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (power up the projector), intransitive (it powered up on its own)

entries.meaning: To go on with a plan although people object or conditions are bad. ---
examples: The city pressed ahead with the bike lanes despite two lawsuits.
They say they will press ahead whatever the survey shows.
Management is pressing ahead with the layoffs.
entries.русский: продолжать, продолжить начатое; настойчиво осуществлять, осуществить
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the plan takes with: pressed ahead with the merger; never ✗ press the merger ahead
entries.forms: press ahead · pressed ahead · pressed ahead

entries.meaning: To keep asking firmly for something until you get it. ---
examples: Reporters pressed for details and got none.
The union is pressing for a raise.
If they press for a decision tonight, say no.
entries.русский: добиваться, добиться (настойчиво); требовать, потребовать
entries.separable: inseparable — for never lets go of its object: pressed for an answer, pressed for it; never ✗ pressed an answer for. The person pressed goes before it: pressed him for details
entries.forms: press for · pressed for · pressed for

entries.meaning: To keep going even though it is hard or discouraging. ---
examples: It was getting dark, but we pressed on.
The team will press on without her.
They are pressing on with the renovation anyway.
entries.русский: продолжать, продолжить (несмотря ни на что); не останавливаться
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; what you continue takes with: pressed on with the search; never ✗ press the search on
entries.forms: press on · pressed on · pressed on

entries.meaning: To take advantage of people who are weak or trusting, usually for money. ---
examples: These schemes prey on people who are desperate.
He preyed on elderly clients for years before anyone checked.
Scammers are preying on students looking for apartments.
entries.русский: наживаться, нажиться (на ком-л.); эксплуатировать (доверчивых); охотиться (на)
entries.separable: inseparable — on keeps its object: prey on the elderly, prey on them; never ✗ prey the elderly on
entries.forms: prey on · preyed on · preyed on

entries.meaning: To produce a paper copy of something from a computer. ---
examples: Print out two copies and bring them with you.
She printed the boarding passes out at the hotel.
He is printing out the directions now.
entries.русский: распечатывать, распечатать; выводить, вывести на печать
entries.separable: separable — print out the form, print the form out, print it out; never ✗ print out it
entries.forms: print out · printed out · printed out

entries.meaning: To keep something from falling by putting a support under it. ---
examples: He propped up the tomato plants with bamboo stakes.
She propped herself up on one elbow.
They are propping up the ceiling until the new beam arrives.
entries.русский: подпирать, подпереть; подставлять, подставить опору
entries.separable: separable — prop up the fence, prop the fence up, prop it up; never ✗ prop up it
entries.forms: prop up · propped up · propped up

entries.meaning: To keep something weak going with money or support it could not survive without. ---
examples: Federal loans propped up the airline for two more years.
The whole business is propped up by one big client.
They cannot keep propping it up forever.
entries.русский: поддерживать, поддержать (искусственно); держать на плаву
entries.separable: separable — prop up the economy, prop the economy up, prop it up; never ✗ prop up it
entries.forms: prop up · propped up · propped up

entries.meaning: To try to find out about someone's private business when it is none of yours. ---
examples: I do not mean to pry into your personal life.
The article pried into details nobody needed to know.
She is always prying into what other people earn.
entries.русский: совать нос (в чужие дела); лезть, влезать в личное
entries.separable: inseparable — into keeps its object: pry into her finances, pry into it; never ✗ pry her finances into. With nothing named, the verb stands alone: I do not mean to pry
entries.forms: pry into · pried into · pried into

entries.meaning: To get information or money from someone who does not want to give it. ---
examples: I finally pried the story out of her.
You will never pry a straight answer out of that office.
He is still prying details out of the witness.
entries.русский: вытягивать, вытянуть (информацию); выпытывать, выпытать
entries.separable: what you get sits in the middle and the person follows out of — pry the truth out of him, pry it out of her; never ✗ pry out of her the truth
entries.forms: pry out of · pried out of · pried out of
entries.third person: pries out of · -ing form: prying out of

entries.meaning: To make an opponent lose confidence by getting inside their head. ---
examples: He tried to psych me out before the match even started.
Their goalie psyched out the whole lineup.
Do not let the crowd psych you out.
entries.русский: сбивать, сбить с толку (психологически); выводить, вывести из равновесия; деморализовать
entries.separable: separable — psych out the other team, psych the other team out, psych him out; never ✗ psych out him
entries.forms: psych out · psyched out · psyched out

entries.meaning: To get yourself or someone else mentally ready and eager for something hard. ---
examples: He psyched himself up for the interview all morning.
The coach knows how to psych up a nervous team.
I have been psyching myself up to call her.
entries.русский: настраивать, настроить (себя); подбадривать, подбодрить; заводить, завести
entries.separable: separable, and usually reflexive — psych yourself up, psych the team up, psych them up; never ✗ psych up them
entries.forms: psych up · psyched up · psyched up

entries.meaning: To push your lips forward, ready to kiss someone. ---
examples: He closed his eyes and puckered up.
Pucker up — the camera is on us.
She is puckering up for the photo.
entries.русский: складывать, сложить губы (для поцелуя); вытягивать, вытянуть губы трубочкой
entries.separable: no object — intransitive, with the lips understood: pucker up. Name the lips and you are back to the plain verb: pucker your lips
entries.forms: pucker up · puckered up · puckered up

entries.meaning: To make your chest or cheeks swell out with air. ---
examples: He puffed out his chest and marched in.
The bird puffs its feathers out when it is cold.
She stood there puffing out her cheeks like a chipmunk.
entries.русский: выпячивать, выпятить (грудь); надувать, надуть (щёки)
entries.separable: separable — puff out his chest, puff his chest out, puff it out; never ✗ puff out it
entries.forms: puff out · puffed out · puffed out

entries.meaning: To swell up, or to make something swell. ---
examples: My eye puffed up after the bee sting.
The bread puffs up in the last five minutes of baking.
She was puffing the pillows up when I walked in.
entries.русский: раздуваться, раздуться; опухать, опухнуть; взбивать, взбить
entries.separable: usually no object — the thing that swells is the subject: her eye puffed up. With an object it separates: puff up the pillows, puff them up
entries.forms: puff up · puffed up · puffed up
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (his ankle puffed up), transitive (puff up the cushions)

entries.meaning: To move into the lead in a race, a game or a contest. ---
examples: She pulled ahead on the last lap.
The challenger has pulled ahead in three straight polls.
They are pulling ahead by two runs.
entries.русский: вырываться, вырваться вперёд; выходить, выйти вперёд
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the rival you pass takes of: pulled ahead of the incumbent; never ✗ pull the incumbent ahead
entries.forms: pull ahead · pulled ahead · pulled ahead

entries.meaning: To start moving off, as a car, bus or train leaving a stop does. ---
examples: The bus pulled away just as we got to the corner.
He pulls away from the curb without even looking.
We watched the train pulling away.
entries.русский: отъезжать, отъехать; трогаться, тронуться (с места)
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the place you leave takes from: pulled away from the curb; never ✗ pull the bus away
entries.forms: pull away · pulled away · pulled away

entries.meaning: To withdraw from something, or to do less of it than before. ---
examples: The company pulled back on hiring after the first quarter.
Advertisers are pulling back from the platform.
They have pulled their forces back to the border.
entries.русский: отступать, отступить; сворачивать, свернуть (деятельность); сокращать, сократить
entries.separable: usually no object — intransitive: investors pulled back, pull back from the edge. With troops or forces named it separates: pulled its forces back
entries.forms: pull back · pulled back · pulled back
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (advertisers pulled back), transitive (pulled the troops back)

entries.meaning: To earn a certain amount of money, especially a large one, in informal American English. ---
examples: She pulls down six figures at that firm.
He was pulling down more as a bartender than as a teacher.
They pulled down record profits last quarter.
entries.русский: зарабатывать, заработать (много); получать, получить (о зарплате)
entries.separable: the amount almost always follows the particle — pulls down six figures; a pronoun can sit in the middle (pulls it down) but that is rare
entries.forms: pull down · pulled down · pulled down

entries.meaning: To knock a building down on purpose. ---
examples: They pulled down the old hotel last spring.
The city wants to pull the whole block down.
Crews have been pulling down houses on that street for a year.
entries.русский: сносить, снести (здание); разрушать, разрушить
entries.separable: separable — pull down the barn, pull the barn down, pull it down; never ✗ pull down it
entries.forms: pull down · pulled down · pulled down

entries.meaning: To hope hard that someone succeeds, and to let them know it. ---
examples: The whole office is pulling for you.
We pulled for the underdog all season.
She pulls for any team from her home state.
entries.русский: болеть (за кого-л.); поддерживать, поддержать; желать удачи
entries.separable: inseparable — for keeps its object: pulling for you, pull for the underdog; never ✗ pull you for
entries.forms: pull for · pulled for · pulled for

entries.meaning: To arrive somewhere and stop, as a train, bus or car does. ---
examples: The bus pulled in twenty minutes late.
We pull in around six if traffic is decent.
Her car was pulling in just as I left.
entries.русский: прибывать, прибыть (о поезде, машине); подъезжать, подъехать
entries.separable: no object in this sense — intransitive; the place takes at or into: pulled in at midnight, pulled into the station
entries.forms: pull in · pulled in · pulled in

entries.meaning: To attract a large number of people, or bring in a large amount of money. ---
examples: The festival pulls in forty thousand people a weekend.
That campaign pulled in a lot of new customers.
They are pulling in more revenue than ever.
entries.русский: привлекать, привлечь (публику); собирать, собрать (аудиторию, деньги)
entries.separable: separable — pull in a crowd, pull the crowd in, pull them in; never ✗ pull in them
entries.forms: pull in · pulled in · pulled in

entries.meaning: To leave a highway, usually to stop for gas, food or a rest. ---
examples: Let us pull off at the next exit.
We pulled off the interstate to find a bathroom.
He was pulling off the road when the engine died.
entries.русский: съезжать, съехать (с трассы); сворачивать, свернуть (с дороги)
entries.separable: inseparable in this sense — the road follows the particle: pull off the highway, pull off at the next exit; never ✗ pull the highway off. With no road named it stands alone: let us pull off and eat
entries.forms: pull off · pulled off · pulled off
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (we pulled off for gas), transitive (pulled off the interstate)

entries.meaning: To manage to do something difficult that people doubted you could do. ---
examples: I do not know how she pulled it off, but the party was perfect.
They pulled off an upset in the final seconds.
Somehow we are pulling it off.
entries.русский: проворачивать, провернуть; справляться, справиться (с трудным); осуществлять, осуществить
entries.separable: separable — pull off a win, pull the deal off, pull it off; never ✗ pull off it. The commonest shape of all is pull it off
entries.forms: pull off · pulled off · pulled off

entries.meaning: To put on a piece of clothing with a quick tug. ---
examples: He pulled on a sweater and headed out into the cold.
Pull your boots on — the yard is still muddy.
She was pulling on her gloves as the elevator doors closed.
entries.русский: натягивать, натянуть (одежду); надевать, надеть
entries.separable: separable — pull on your boots, pull your boots on, pull them on; never ✗ pull on them
entries.forms: pull on · pulled on · pulled on

entries.meaning: To drive out of a parking space or side road into moving traffic. ---
examples: He pulled out right in front of me.
Wait for the bus to pull out before you cross.
She is pulling out of the driveway now.
entries.русский: выезжать, выехать (на дорогу); трогаться, тронуться с места
entries.separable: no object — intransitive; the road takes into or onto, and the car you cut off takes in front of: pulled out in front of a bus
entries.forms: pull out · pulled out · pulled out

entries.meaning: To stop taking part in something you had agreed to. ---
examples: Two sponsors pulled out a week before the show.
They are threatening to pull out of the agreement.
The country has pulled most of its troops out.
entries.русский: выходить, выйти (из соглашения); отказываться, отказаться от участия; выводить, вывести (войска)
entries.separable: usually no object — intransitive, and what you leave takes of: pulled out of the deal. With troops or money named it separates: pulled its troops out
entries.forms: pull out · pulled out · pulled out
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (two sponsors pulled out), transitive (pulled their troops out)

entries.meaning: To move a vehicle to the side of the road and stop. ---
examples: Pull over — I think we have a flat.
She pulled over to answer the phone.
He was pulling over when the tire blew.
entries.русский: съезжать, съехать на обочину; останавливаться, остановиться у обочины
entries.separable: usually no object — just pull over here. When the vehicle is named it separates: pull the car over, pull it over; never ✗ pull over it
entries.forms: pull over · pulled over · pulled over
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (we pulled over), transitive (pull the truck over)

entries.meaning: To signal a driver to stop at the roadside, as the police do. ---
examples: A trooper pulled us over just past the state line.
He has been pulled over twice this month.
They pull people over for that all the time.
entries.русский: останавливать, остановить (машину — о полиции); тормозить, притормозить (водителя)
entries.separable: separable, and the driver or car normally sits in the middle — pulled me over, pulled the truck over; never ✗ pulled over me
entries.forms: pull over · pulled over · pulled over

entries.meaning: To survive a serious illness or get safely through a very bad time. ---
examples: It was touch and go, but she pulled through.
The doctors say he will pull through.
We have pulled through worse than this.
entries.русский: выкарабкиваться, выкарабкаться; выживать, выжить; справляться, справиться (с бедой)
entries.separable: usually no object — intransitive: the doctors think he will pull through. When something carries the person, it splits: her sense of humor pulled her through
entries.forms: pull through · pulled through · pulled through
entries.transitivity: both — intransitive (she pulled through), transitive (music pulled him through)

entries.meaning: To get control of your emotions again after being upset. ---
examples: Give me a minute to pull myself together.
She pulled herself together and finished the speech.
He is still pulling himself together after the news.
entries.русский: брать, взять себя в руки; успокаиваться, успокоиться
entries.separable: always separable and always reflexive — the pronoun goes in the middle: pull yourself together, pulled himself together; never ✗ pull together yourself
entries.forms: pull together · pulled together · pulled together
entries.transitivity: transitive — always with a reflexive object (myself, yourself, herself)

entries.meaning: To put something together quickly out of separate pieces. ---
examples: Can you pull together a one-page summary by noon?
She pulled a whole dinner together in half an hour.
We are pulling together the numbers for the board.
entries.русский: собирать, собрать (воедино); готовить, подготовить (быстро)
entries.separable: separable — pull together a proposal, pull the proposal together, pull it together; never ✗ pull together it
entries.forms: pull together · pulled together · pulled together

entries.meaning: To work as one group toward the same goal, especially in a hard time. ---
examples: The neighborhood pulled together after the flood.
If everyone pulls together, we will finish by Friday.
They are pulling together the way a good team does.
entries.русский: действовать сообща; сплачиваться, сплотиться; объединять, объединить усилия
entries.separable: no object in this sense — intransitive: the whole town pulled together; never ✗ pull the town together with this meaning
entries.forms: pull together · pulled together · pulled together

entries.meaning: To arrive somewhere and come to a stop, as a car does. ---
examples: A black SUV pulled up outside the house.
We pull up at the gate and they wave us through.
He was pulling up just as I left.
entries.русский: подъезжать, подъехать и остановиться; притормаживать, притормозить
entries.separable: no object in this sense — intransitive; the place takes at, to or outside: pulled up outside the school; never ✗ pull the curb up
entries.forms: pull up · pulled up · pulled up
